prompt:
A photograph of a newspaper page's chess-variant column, square on, the column filling the frame in newsprint halftone.

The column is headed 'THE SENTRY PROBLEM'. A boxed paragraph under the heading gives the piece rule, word for word: 'THE SENTRY moves and attacks like a rook, any number of empty squares along a rank or file, and it ALSO attacks the four squares diagonally adjacent to it. Any piece standing in its straight-line path blocks it. Kings move as in chess. A king may not capture a defended piece and the two kings may never stand on adjacent squares.'

Below the box sits the problem DIAGRAM: a printed eight-by-eight board with file letters a to h and rank numbers 1 to 8 on its margins, carrying exactly THREE pieces -- the white king, one white Sentry and the black king. Beneath the diagram sits ONE caption line in the column's house format, exactly: 'White: K__, S__. Black: K__. Mate.' with the three squares filled in.

This week's composition commission: place the three pieces so that the BLACK KING IS CHECKMATED by the Sentry -- its own square attacked, every square beside it attacked or illegal to enter. Work the placement out yourself -- I am deliberately not telling you where any piece stands; composing the mate is the commission. The diagram and the caption must show the same position. Do not print any analysis, move list or extra line: the only text in the column is the heading, the boxed rule, the diagram's margin coordinates and the one caption line, all readable.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a printed page with a chessboard diagram, a text box and a caption line? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a plain diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image shows just a bare card of text with no board diagram, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_cap_cert: Does this cut-out show one printed caption line naming chess squares, rather than the heading or the rule box? Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: the caption line printed directly beneath the board diagram

steps.read_crop: Copy the caption line in this cut-out exactly as printed. Write nothing else.

steps.target: one chess piece symbol printed on the board diagram

steps.read_crop: Does this cut-out show ONE whole chess piece symbol on a board square, rather than a margin letter or an empty square? Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: a printed line of move analysis or a second caption below the one caption line
